player draft | organized = [[Canadian Hockey League]] (CHL) | website = {{URL|http://www.chl.ca/draft/}} }} The '''CHL Import Draft''' is an annual event in which every team in the [[Canadian Hockey League]] (CHL) may select the rights to eligible import players. An import is classified as a player who does not have residency status in either Canada or the United States. The draft is conducted online, during the last week of June, or first week of July, following the [[NHL entry draft]]. Teams from the [[Western Hockey League]], [[Ontario Hockey League]], and [[Quebec Maritimes Junior Hockey League]], systematically take turns making selections. Teams can have a maximum of two imports which may only be obtained through the draft. The draft is open to all position players, but a ban on drafting European goalkeepers was in effect from 2014 to 2017. As of the 2025 draft, 2,380 players have been selected, with many later going onto the [[National Hockey League]]. ==History and process== The CHL Import Draft began in 1992.{{cite web|url=http://www.eliteprospects.com/draft_other.php?type=CHL%20Import%20Draft|title=CHL Import Draft|website=Elite Prospects|access-date=November 3, 2025}} It is an annual event in which every team in the [[Canadian Hockey League]] (CHL) may select the rights to eligible import players. An import is classified as a player who does not have residency status in either Canada or the United States. The draft is conducted online, during the last week of June, or first week of July, following the [[NHL entry draft]].{{cite news|url=http://torontosun.com/sports/hockey/if-chl-lifts-european-goalie-ban-it-would-not-be-about-righting-a-wrong-branch|title=David Branch says lifting European goalie ban would not be about CHL righting a wrong|last=Matisz|first=John|date=February 24, 2018|newspaper=Toronto Sun|access-date= December 27, 2022}} Teams from the [[Western Hockey League]] (WHL), [[Ontario Hockey League]] (OHL), and [[Quebec Maritimes Junior Hockey League]] (QMJHL), systematically take turns making selections in reverse order of the team's standings in the CHL from the previous season. Teams can have a maximum of two imports which may only be obtained through the draft,{{cite web|url=http://hockeyfamilyadvisor.com/draft-eligibility-juniormajor-junior-chl/|title=Draft & Eligibility – Major Junior – CHL|last=MacDonald|first=David|date=September 23, 2012|website=Hockey Family Advisor|access-date=January 19, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180121071318/http://hockeyfamilyadvisor.com/draft-eligibility-juniormajor-junior-chl/|archive-date=2018-01-21|url-status=dead}} and teams must have an open roster space for an import player before a draft selection is made, otherwise they must pass on the opportunity.{{cite web|url=https://thehockeywriters.com/chl-import-draft-highlights/|title=CHL Import Draft Highlights|last=Langridge|first=Jeff|date=June 29, 2017|website=The Hockey Writers|access-date=January 19, 2018}} As of the 2025 draft, 2,380 players have been selected, with many later going onto the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL). The majority of imported players come from the Czech Republic, Russia, and Slovakia. ==Inherent risk assessment== The Import Draft has inherent risks that teams must assess, before making a draft pick which costs $2,000 up front.{{cite web|url=http://www.stcatharinesstandard.ca/2013/06/17/new-rules-for-import-goalies|title=OHL says no to import goalies|last=Potrecz|first=Bill|date=2013-06-17|website=St. Catharines Standard|access-date=2018-01-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180120235928/http://www.stcatharinesstandard.ca/2013/06/17/new-rules-for-import-goalies|archive-date=2018-01-20|url-status=dead}} Drafted players may choose not to report, therefore teams want to be certain a player will. Potential draftees have often been previously chosen in the NHL entry draft, and thus have an incentive to report to a CHL team because NHL teams want prospects closer for development. Also, there is more exposure to scouts in North America for imports not drafted by an NHL team. Competition with the [[KHL Junior Draft]] for the same player is also an obstacle.{{cite web|url=https://www.puckworlds.com/2010/6/30/1544388/chl-import-draft-is-major-junior|title=CHL Import Draft: Is Major Junior the right path for Europeans?|last=Peter|first=Bruce|date=2010-06-30|website=Puck Worlds|access-date=2018-01-19}} Imported players usually prefer playing in the CHL instead of the [[United States Hockey League]] (USHL), due to the higher level of competition.{{cite web|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ca/nhl/news/chl-import-draft-prospect-ranking-top-five-matvei-guskov-mikko-kokkonen/1ukur9zi2e4e712u2j5c7m03ir|title=Top prospects ranked for 2018 CHL Import Draft|last=Mahiban|first=Dhiren|date=2018-01-26|website=Sporting News|access-date=2018-06-28}} Most CHL teams have contacted few players in advance of the draft.{{cite web|url=http://www.hockeysfuture.com/articles/126003/chl-import-draft-zacha-prime-example-import-drafting-success-plus-review-2015-draft/|title=CHL Import Draft: Zacha prime example of Import drafting success, plus a review of 2015 draft|last=Hahn|first=David|date=2015-06-30|website=Hockey's Future|access-date=2018-01-19}} Scouting these players is difficult as most teams do not employ European scouts, but rather rely on videos and limited exposure at international tournaments.{{cite web|url=http://www.sportsnet.ca/hockey/juniors/whl-blog-breaking-down-the-chl-import-draft/|title=WHL blog: Breaking down the CHL import draft|last=Eide|first=Andrew|date=2015-07-02|website=Sportsnet.ca|access-date=2018-01-19}} Players may also have professional contracts in European domestic leagues. The current system can be compared to an auction, where teams are bidding for services in competition with these other leagues, and have to pay large release fees.{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/chl-import-draft--can-new-rule-changes-fix-a-broken-system---194409144.html|title=CHL Import Draft: Can new rule changes fix a broken system?|last=Sapurji|first=Sunaya|date=2013-02-07|website=Yahoo! Sports|access-date=2018-01-19}} Once an import draftee reports to a CHL team, there is also risk involved in whether the player adapts to being far away from home, the ability to speak [[English language|English]] or [[French language|French]], playing on smaller ice surfaces, and the more physical North American game. There is a year-long moratorium on trading the pick, once in the CHL, which is to prevent bidding for services by larger market clubs. One benefit of selecting an import player before he is drafted into the NHL, is that he is treated like a North American player in the sense that he will either have to play in the CHL or NHL, and not in the [[American Hockey League]].{{cite web|url=https://www.guelphmercury.com/sports-story/7393890-from-the-stands-guelph-storm-looks-at-chl-import-draft/|title=From the Stands: Guelph Storm looks at CHL Import Draft|last=Osborne|first=Paul|date=2017-06-27|website=GuelphMercury.com|access-date=2018-01-19}} ==Eligibility and residency== Teams may choose any player who meets age requirements, and resides outside of the normal territorial claims for the entry draft of the constituent leagues. To avoid the Import Draft, foreign-born players have come to play [[minor hockey]] in Canada or the United States and earn local status.{{cite web|url=http://www.thehockeynews.com/news/article/in-a-global-world-who-still-counts-as-an-import|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180121005242/http://www.thehockeynews.com/section/news|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 21, 2018|title=In a global hockey world, who still counts as an import?|last=Kennedy|first=Ryan|date=2017-09-15|website=The Hockey News|access-date=2018-01-19}}{{cite web|url=http://lastwordonhockeyprospects.com/2018/03/03/numbers-chls-ban-import-goalies-worked/|title=By the Numbers: How has the CHL's Import Draft ban on Goalies worked?|last=Thiel|first=Bryan|date=2018-03-03|website=Last Word on Hockey Prospects|access-date=2018-06-28}} Draft eligibility is based on the parents’ full-time residence, by looking at housing deeds, banking records, or lease agreements, rather than the length of time spent in the country. Cases for local status are dealt with individually by the CHL. Examples of foreign-born players classified as locals include [[David Levin (ice hockey)|David Levin]] from [[Israel]], [[Daniel Sprong]] from the [[Netherlands]], and [[Alex Galchenyuk]] who was born in [[Wisconsin]] of a [[Belarus]]ian father. Examples of players denied local status include [[Ivan Provorov]] and [[Toronto Maple Leafs]] prospect Nikita Korostelev from Russia, and [[Tampa Bay Lightning]] prospect Dennis Yan, despite being born in [[Oregon]]. Teams from the QMJHL have fewer American states to choose from compared to the WHL and OHL, and use the import draft to build competitive rosters. The New England states also see tough competition from [[NCAA Division I]] colleges for the same players. {|class="wikitable" |+Territorial claims of the Canadian Hockey League{{cite web|last=MacDonald|first=David|date=2013-03-29|title=Understanding the CHL's Major Junior Draft Process|url=http://hockeyfamilyadvisor.com/understanding-the-chls-major-junior-draft-process/|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180121071500/http://hockeyfamilyadvisor.com/understanding-the-chls-major-junior-draft-process/|archive-date=2018-01-21|access-date=2018-01-20|website=Hockey Family Advisor}}{{cite web|last=Olynyk|first=Nick|date=2014|title=How To Get Picked In The OHL Draft|url=http://juniorhockeytruth.com/ohl-draft/|access-date=2018-01-20|website=Junior Hockey Truth}} |- align="center" ! [[Prince Edward Island]], [[Newfoundland and Labrador]] || All New England states |} ==European goalkeeper ban== On June 11, 2013, the CHL announced that the upcoming Import Draft would be the final opportunity to select European goalkeepers.{{cite web|url=http://chl.ca/chl-announces-import-draft-change|title=CHL announces Import Draft change|date=2013-06-11|website=Canadian Hockey League|access-date=2018-01-19}} Teams could draft 1994 or 1995 birth-year goalkeepers only in the first round of the 2013 Import Draft, and current import goalkeepers in the CHL would remain eligible to continue playing until the standard age limit. The CHL cited the need to improve Canadian goalkeeping as a reason behind the change. The move is seen as a response to [[Hockey Canada]]'s recent inability to develop top notch goaltenders.{{cite web|url=https://www.nhl.com/news/chl-moving-to-ban-european-goalies/c-673607|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160807013411/https://www.nhl.com/news/chl-moving-to-ban-european-goalies/c-673607|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 7, 2016|title=CHL moving to ban European goalies|last=Kimelman|first=Adam|date=2013-06-12|website=NHL.com|access-date=2018-01-19}}{{cite web|url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/hockey/2013/06/11/chl_officially_moves_to_ban_import_goalies_cox.html|title=CHL officially moves to ban import goalies|last=Cox|first=Damien|date=2013-06-11|website=Toronto Star|access-date=2018-01-19}} The [[Canada men's national junior ice hockey team|Canadian junior team]] had not won a [[IIHF World Junior Championship|World Junior Championship]] since 2009, which was blamed on poor goalkeeping. Other signs of Canada's goalkeeper weakness include: the 2013 [[CHL Goaltender of the Year]] award went to [[Patrik Bartošák|Patrik Bartosak]] of the Czech Republic,{{cite web|url=http://chl.ca/chl-awards|title=CHL Awards|website=chl.ca|publisher=Canadian Hockey League|access-date=2017-12-24}} all three [[Vezina Trophy]] finalists in the [[2012–13 NHL season]] were Europeans,{{cite web|url=http://hockeygoalies.org/awards/vezinavoting.php|title=Vezina Trophy Voting History: Year-by-year|website=Hockey Goalies|access-date=2018-01-20}} and a Canadian had not been the first goalkeeper chosen in the NHL Entry Draft in five years. Arguments were made that Canadian goalkeepers were not getting a chance to develop, and that teams contending for a championship were drafting goaltenders from Europe. The change may actually benefit the banned goalkeepers, as statistics indicate that the best European goalkeepers have been developed in their own domestic leagues.{{cite web|url=http://www.iihf.com/home-of-hockey/news/news-singleview/?tx_ttnews%5Btt_news%5D=8007&cHash=e9f4bdc1da380f8b7a2d2ed2af41ec85|title=CHL gets it right on goalies|last=Aykroyd|first=Lucas|date=2013-06-19 |website=International Ice Hockey Federation|access-date=2018-01-19}} The CHL began reevaluating the ban in February 2018, in cooperation with Hockey Canada. Commissioner [[David Branch (ice hockey)|David Branch]] said that the ban was never viewed as a mistake, and its reversal was not trying to right a wrong; rather it was about comparing the development programs since put in place to best serve the interest of the Canadian goalkeeper. [[USA Hockey]] has implemented similar programs, and the USHL recently slackened its import player rules, allowing more Canadians and Europeans. The proposal to resume drafting European goalkeepers claims that it brings more competition, and forces Canadians to prove their talents against a broader pool. In the four NHL Entry Drafts since the ban was implemented, 36 goalkeepers have been selected from Europe, 26 from elsewhere in North America ([[National Collegiate Athletic Association]], USHL, [[North American Hockey League]]), and 22 from the CHL. For the 2018 draft, the ban was lifted and European goalkeepers became eligible again for selection.{{cite web|url=http://chl.ca/article/2018-chl-import-draft-set-for-thursday-june-28|title=2018 CHL Import Draft set for Thursday June 28|date=2018-06-27|website=Canadian Hockey League|access-date=2018-06-28}}{{cite web|url=http://whl.ca/article/2018-chl-import-draft-set-for-thursday-june-28|title=2018 CHL Import Draft set for Thursday June 28|date=2018-06-27|website=WHL.ca|access-date=2018-06-27}} ==Draft selections by origin== List of CHL Import Draft selections, organized by [[List of members of the International Ice Hockey Federation|International Ice Hockey Federation member association]] of origin. extract: The CHL Import Draft is an annual event in which every team in the Canadian Hockey League (CHL) may select the rights to  eligible import players. An import is classified as a player who does not have residency status in either Canada or the United States. The draft is conducted online, during the last week of June, or first week of July, following the NHL entry draft. Teams from the Western Hockey League, Ontario Hockey League, and Quebec Maritimes Junior Hockey League, systematically take turns making selections. Teams can have a maximum of two imports which may only be obtained through the draft. The draft is open to all position players, but a ban on drafting European goalkeepers was in effect from 2014 to 2017. As of the 2025 draft, 2,380 players have been selected, with many later going onto the National Hockey League.
